title: We Manufacture Our Own Masters · Why read this book?
description: The mechanism through which a political ideal succeeds can produce its opposite, so free orders must be judged under hostile leadership and protected by testable counterpowers rather than goodwill.

readerInvitation.reasonToExist: Confiscate every fortune, and someone still decides who gets a home and who may leave. We Manufacture Our Own Masters calls these traps antinomies, and finds them in every camp. The author knew them from communism, where levelled incomes still hid a nobility without titles.
readerInvitation.readerPromise: The mechanism through which a political ideal succeeds can produce its opposite, so free orders must be judged under hostile leadership and protected by testable counterpowers rather than goodwill.
readerInvitation.audienceFit: readers of political philosophy, institutional design and technology policy who distrust both utopias and easy cynicism
readerInvitation.closingInvitation: Begin with chapter one, Antinomies Are Not Accidents, and run its test on your favourite system.
readerOutcomes: Its test is adversarial: judge each system by what a hostile leader could do.
Then ask how the people affected could stop that leader.
Liberalism, Chinese order, private cities and guaranteed income all face the same scrutiny.
